title: Using Localization To Increase Player Base
author: YuukiCrypto
selftext:
One of the greatest benefits of AI is its ability to break down language barriers. Something I am already putting into my game design document is localization.

  
I am planning ahead. Every "monster" in my game will have an easily translated version. When naming the different creatures you can collect, I am considering how that translates - and how memorable those words will be in another language.

  
AI game dev is easily set apart from regular game development because you instantly get access to features you never would have been able to do without this technology.

  
I develop web apps in my spare time and one of my best selling tools did so well because I was able to sell internationally. It took one prompt and 30 minutes to get the software I worked years on into multiple languages. From there it was very easy to get sales from across the world.

  
The same rule applies here. If you want to increase your player count, you should not limit yourself to English speaking players.

  
In addition, other countries are much more open to interacting with Artificial Intelligence.

  
A lot of game developers do not understand marketing so take my advice. Localization is one of your strongest marketing tools and AI enables you to use it. Most AAA games don't even release in multiple languages, so you already know the same applies to indie games.

  
Stand out. Plan for other markets.

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
Localization is also critical to think about in the early design phases.  One of the most common mistakes indie devs make is to have everything in their game hard coded in their native language.

All text should be a keyed reference.  That way you just swap out what's referenced and it prints in the language it's set to.  Localization becomes a game of getting a quality translation and QAing for differences in text length, not painstakingly going through every line of game code and engine object manually changing lines of text.
